title: BPISC: bounded proportional-integral surge controller for dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background:
Redwood Dedicated customers require predictable throughput and controlled cost during bursts. Existing controllers either over-provision (high cost) or oscillate (SLO violations). This ticket introduces BPISC — a bounded proportional-integral surge controller — designed to target multi-signal objectives while enforcing strict safety limits for fleets serving dedicated customers.

Goals:
- Provide a single autoscaling policy artifact that balances p95 latency SLOs, tenant throughput guarantees, and cost headroom.
- Use multi-signal inputs (p95 latency, tokens/sec, queue depth, KV cache hit ratio, per-tenant credit balance) to compute scaling intent.
- Enforce hard safety fences: max_surge, slew_rate, warmup_budget, and eviction thresholds.
- Make the policy auditable, tunable via runtime flags, and rolloutable as a canary.

Core design (high level):
- Target metrics: p95 latency (primary), tokens/sec (throughput), active-concurrency, KV cache hit ratio (efficiency), and cost-per-token estimate. Each metric is normalized into a unitless signal and weighted by tenant SLA and fleet profile.
- Controller algorithm: bounded proportional-integral loop with quantile anchoring and probe-based warmup: BPISC uses a conservative proportional term tuned to p95 overshoot, an integral term with decay to avoid windup during long plateaus, and a bounded output limiter derived from available surge_budget.
- Surge budgeting: maintain a ledger per-fleet of surge_credits that are consumed when BPISC issues scale-up beyond the steady-state target. Credits replenish slowly based on utilization and reserved headroom policies.
- Safety limits: global max_surge (absolute GPU slots), per-tenant cap, slew_rate (max delta slots per minute), probe timeouts (grace period for warm instances), and rollback triggers (error rate > 2x baseline or sustained p99 regressions).

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive PID tuning improves latency recovery but increases cost and risk of oscillation. We bias toward stability for Dedicated customers and provide knobs for more aggressive modes via fleet profiles.
- Using more signals (cache hit ratio, cost) improves economics but adds complexity to telemetry; we include fallbacks that degrade gracefully when a signal is missing.

Acceptance criteria (summary):
- Under synthetic burst tests, p95 latency remains <= configured SLO in >= 97% of windows while cost overhead over baseline <= 25% for 95% of trials.
- Controller respects slew_rate and max_surge; no rollout should ever allocate > max_surge physical slots.
- Canary rollout: successful canary across 3 tenants with differing traffic shapes and auto-rollback on rollback-trigger conditions.

Rollout plan (brief):
1) Unit tests + simulator run (local) against trace corpus (see links).
2) Staging rollout to internal dedicated fleet (non-prod) for 48h.
3) Canary to 3 small paying customers (with opt-in) for 72h.
4) Full gradual rollout with feature flag and 1-hour monitoring window for auto-rollback.

Metrics to instrument:
- p50/p95/p99 latency per-tenant, tokens/sec, active_slots, allocated_slots, surge_credits_balance, KV cache hit ratio, error rates, scaling decisions per-minute.

Implementation notes:
- Implementation will live in autoscaler/service with a new strategy class bpisc.Strategy. It will read weighted signals from metric-bridge and use the capacity allocator to request slot changes. The strategy must be deterministic (no random seeds in decision path) to allow replay in simulator.
- Provide an HTTP debug endpoint exposing recent decision history (last 200 decisions) and contributing signal weights for audit.

Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood-inference.internal/display/DED/BPISC+Design+Doc
- Simulator traces and results: https://internal-redwood.storage/simulations/bpisc/2026-03-04-results.csv
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood-inference.internal/d/bpisc/autoscale-debug
- Initial PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/421
comments: 2026-03-06 — Initial spec posted. Reviewed with runtime and product; runtime asked for deterministic decision logs and a bounded integral to avoid windup during long spikes. Action: add decay parameter to integral term. — Aisha
2026-03-08 — Engineering sync: agreed to reuse surge_credits ledger from ENG-631210 (debt ticket) rather than invent new accounting. Assignee to prototype ledger adapter. — Mateo
2026-03-10 — Review from Product (Lena Cho): validated acceptance criteria for p95 and cost overhead; requested a canary checklist and customer opt-in flow. Added to rollout plan. — Product
2026-03-11 — PR 421 opened (WIP). CI failing on integration test that simulates warmup under KV pressure. Investigating race between probe-warmup and cache priming. — Mateo

2026-03-12 — Decided: set default fleet profile to "stable-conservative" for P0 customers; allow "burst-optimistic" for opt-in fleets. Added flags: bpisc.integral_decay and bpisc.max_surge_fraction. — Aisha
acceptance_criteria: Automated simulator shows p95 SLO met >=97% across synthetic traces within cost bounds
No allocation exceeds max_surge during canary and staged rollout
Rollback triggers reliably detect regression and revert to previous policy within configured window
Decision logs and debug endpoint provide explainability for each scale event
test_plan: Unit tests for bpisc.Strategy: proportional, integral with decay, and bounds enforcement
Simulator runs across 12 traffic traces with randomized tenant mixes
Integration test against staging metric-bridge and allocator using short-lived traces
Canary run with monitoring alerts and automated rollback in place
